speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: By 2030, eight in 10 households will be within a 10-minute walk of a train station.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The advent of sharing services of active mobility devices, such as bicycles, power-assisted bicycles (PABs) and personal mobility devices (PMDs), has made the journey between the train station and our homes and workplaces even more convenient.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Over time, we will reduce our reliance on cars.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Today, two in three trips during peak periods are already made on public transport.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: By 2030, we aim for three in four trips to be so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: We will continue to work towards a car-lite Singapore, which will allow us to maximise the use of limited land and free up car park spaces for other uses, such as housing, schools and hospitals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: This Bill will support our vision of a car-lite Singapore by making two key changes to the Parking Places Act (PPA).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: While such sharing operations contribute to the attractiveness of our public transport network, it was unfortunate that it has led to pervasive indiscriminate parking of bicycles which degrades our living environment and creates safety issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: A licensing regime will address the problem of indiscriminate parking and allow sharing operations to grow in a more sustainable manner.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: This will, in turn, allow us to maximise the use of the limited land in Singapore and free up space to improve our living environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The first set of amendments pertains to the licensing of dockless vehicle-sharing operators.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: There are many advantages to dockless bicycle sharing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: First, it omits the need to build expensive docks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Second, it provides the convenience for Singaporeans who wish to use a bicycle occasionally, but do not want the hassle of owning one.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Third, users can pick up the bicycle at the start of a journey and drop it off at the end, which is very convenient and offers Singaporeans more travel options.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: This has, in turn, helped to encourage active mobility in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Unfortunately, indiscriminate parking of shared bicycles has marred this positive development.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The bicycle sharing operators have exacerbated this problem as they grew their fleets too quickly in a bid to capture market share.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: There are also inconsiderate and irresponsible users who leave bicycles outside of the designated parking spaces.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) has worked hard to address the problem.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: LTA has been increasing parking infrastructure for bicycles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: There are now over 170,000 public bicycle parking lots at Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) stations, bus stops, HDB estates and parks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: LTA and other public agencies plan to provide another 50,000 more bicycle parking lots by 2020.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Collectively, they provide ease of accessibility without cluttering our urban landscape, a balance we need to strike even if some users prefer bicycle parking lots right at their doorstep.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: LTA, the National Parks Board (NParks) and Town Councils have also signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with bicycle-sharing operators in October 2017.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The MOU contains guidelines for the responsible operation of bicycle-sharing services in public spaces and educating users on proper parking behaviour.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: In addition, LTA has impounded indiscriminately parked bicycles which were not removed by operators within half a day and fined operators.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Despite these efforts, the problem of indiscriminate parking remains.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: To strengthen LTA's levers to deal with indiscriminate parking, we propose to introduce a licensing framework for active mobility device-sharing operators.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: I have spoken about this during my Ministry’s Committee of Supply (COS) debate earlier this month and many Members in the House have expressed their support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Clause 6 of the Bill introduces a new Part 3, which consists of new sections 8 to 8T setting out the proposed licensing regime.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: It will be an offence to operate without a licence under section 8C.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: If convicted, unlicensed operators will face a fine of up to $10,000, or imprisonment of up to six months, or both.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: A further fine of up to $500 will be imposed for each day the offence continues after conviction.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Next, allow me to elaborate on the scope and key features of the licensing regime.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: First, the licensing regime will cover dockless vehicle-sharing services for active mobility devices, such as bicycles, PMDs and PABs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Second, the regime is focused on sharing services that operate in public places.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Section 8 defines public places as state land and land controlled or managed by a statutory body, where the public has free access.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Vehicle-sharing services that operate only in private land, or in areas where the public does not have free right of access, will not be covered by the licensing regime.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Examples include private land, such as shopping malls, places where access requires proof of identity, such as military camps or ticketed attractions like the Singapore Zoo.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Third, we will not regulate docked vehicle-sharing businesses whose vehicles must be hired from or returned to exclusive vehicle docking stations, such as Vélib in Paris or YouBike in Taipei.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: A bicycle rental business operating from a shop is also excluded from the licensing regime if its customers must return the bicycles hired to the shop.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The nature of such services makes them less likely to cause parking-related disamenities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Given the scale of the indiscriminate parking problem today, LTA will take a more conservative approach in setting the fleet sizes at the start.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: However, we will review the fleet sizes regularly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Operators who manage their fleets well can apply to LTA to grow their fleets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: In assessing applications to increase fleet size, LTA will take into account factors, such as the operator’s ability to manage indiscriminate parking by its users, its fleet utilisation rate, and other relevant factors, such as the demand for the service and availability of parking spaces.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: This will create the right incentives for operators to put in place processes to manage indiscriminate parking and ensure that each operator grows its fleet in a more sustainable manner.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Second, the licensing regime will give LTA regulatory levers to require operators to manage indiscriminate parking.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Under sections 8G, 8H, 8N and 8O, LTA will be able to impose and vary licence conditions on each operator, issue directions, and set industry-wide "standards of performance" on the service provided by licensees.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: For example, under section 8N(2), LTA will set industry-wide standards relating to the use of geofencing and on the frequency of removal of indiscriminately parked vehicles in a timely manner.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Under section 8P, LTA can take regulatory action against operators who fail to comply with its directions, standards of performance or licence conditions, such as the maximum fleet size.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: A range of regulatory action is provided to LTA to enable a better calibrated response to non-compliance by licensees.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Clause 11 also amends section 15 of the PPA to empower appointed enforcement officers to remove and detain abandoned vehicles which were used in the provision of unlicensed vehicle-sharing services or parked in contravention of any written law.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The majority of users are responsible and park the shared vehicles in designated parking areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: However, there are irresponsible and inconsiderate users who do not do so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Under the licensing regime, LTA can direct operators to impose a time-limited ban on users who repeatedly park the shared vehicles indiscriminately.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: To this end, section 8L authorises licensed operators to share among themselves information on users who have improperly parked vehicles in a public place.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The information sharing will be limited to the extent necessary for implementing the collective ban.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: LTA will be able to leverage data and technology to improve enforcement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Section 8K imposes obligations on operators to keep accounts and records, and to provide information to LTA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: This can include data on the location of each deployed vehicle so that LTA can remotely track indiscriminately parked vehicles and enforce more effectively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Section 8M also requires operators to provide information when requested by LTA for enforcement purposes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Failure to provide information to LTA under sections 8K and 8M will be offences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Section 8Q empowers the Minister for Transport to make safety directives to minimise the risk of death or serious injury to individuals, or damage to property arising from dockless vehicle-sharing services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Under section 8R, licensees or licence applicants can appeal to the Minister for Transport against certain LTA decisions under the new Part 3.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Clause 12 inserts a new section 15C to make it an offence to provide false or misleading information in licence applications.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: PPA was last amended in 2005 and needs to be updated to prepare for a time when we will rely less on cars.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Today, PPA allows LTA to make rules on the number of parking places or spaces to be provided on any type of land or buildings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Private developments have to provide a specified minimum number of parking lots.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Clause 17 introduces a new section 22 which empowers LTA to make rules prescribing the range of parking lots which private developers have to provide, defined by a lower and/or upper limit.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: This will enable LTA to better calibrate parking provision requirements for private developments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: LTA will release more details by the end of the year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Clause 5 introduces a new section 6A which allows LTA to approve proposals to provide parking lots in accordance with rules made under the new section 22.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The Bill will also amend the PPA to improve the operational efficiency of HDB and Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) car parks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: This will bring us a step closer to our vision of a car-lite Singapore.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: Cycling is also a healthy and environmentally friendly mode of transport.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: The key concerns which have been received are as follows.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: First, the dangers cyclists and PMD users bring to pedestrians, especially when they travel along footpaths and common areas.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: Second, the dangers they bring to themselves, drivers and riders when they travel recklessly on roads, ignoring traffic rules and basic road etiquette.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: Third, the indiscriminate parking of shared bikes at common areas.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: And fourth, the inconsiderate use of shared bikes, exemplified in the abuse and dumping of shared bikes.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: These have generated not only inconveniences, but also tangible hazards to the health and well-being of our people.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: I wish to propose several measures for LTA to consider to make the use of shared bikes and PMDs a more pleasant experience for all in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: As a result, accidents which have resulted in injuries to pedestrians, cyclists and PMD users have occurred.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: We need to expedite the building of cycling and PMD-friendly paths, especially along LTA's road pavements.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: Where possible, cycling and pedestrian paths should be separate to minimise the risks of accidents.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: These provide enough space to store 28,000 bicycles for our residents and have drastically reduced the indiscriminate parking of shared bikes in our blocks.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: I would also like to draw attention to a pilot project undertaken by the Holland-Bukit Panjang Town Council involving the implementation of Geo-Station technology.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: This has also encouraged shared bike users to park their bikes at the designated yellow boxes in our town.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: Although the increase in the supply of bicycle lots at the HDB void decks has reduced indiscriminate parking, many shared bikes are still left at various places outside and around housing estates.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: At the same time, we hope that LTA and other Government agencies will also expedite the provision of parking places at bus stops, Light Rail Transit (LRT) and MRT stations, parks and public amenities.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: This will ensure the docking of shared bikes at these yellow boxes by all bike sharing users.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: In addition, it is of paramount importance that LTA ensure that regular housekeeping is performed by the bike sharing operators to make sure that shared bikes are properly parked in the yellow boxes.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: Third, enforcement against bike operators, cyclists and PMD users.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: This will ensure that bike sharing operators take measures to maintain a fleet of safe and roadworthy bikes for hire, and adopt appropriate measures, technological or otherwise, to prevent the indiscriminate parking of bikes by the hirers.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: To ensure the safety of all parties, all cyclists and PMD users must slow down and signal in advance to warn pedestrians.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: LTA should also set up mobile enforcement teams to act against reckless cyclists and PMD users based on feedback from the public.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: In the facilitation of enforcement, a telephone hotline to gather information from the public on "hot spots" or accident-prone areas will be of great value.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: The setting up of a hotline will also encourage more people to keep watch on the behaviour of cyclists and PMD users.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: The first is on the role and accountability of the operator to maintain roadworthiness of their vehicles so as to ensure the safety of hirers.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: This particular issue is mentioned under a few sections, such as 8E and 8G, with regard to granting and renewal of licences, and also section 8O under the subheading "Directions".

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: My other point is on section 8K(2), which depicts, "a licensee must keep and retain for such periods, as may be prescribed records, where the records are relevant to the hiring of vehicles from the licensee, their period of hire, the place from which the hire started and ended, and any other prescribed information relating to the hirer or hiring of vehicles used to provide licensable services".

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Though the Bill aims to implement a licensing regime on dockless bicycle-sharing operators to address the problem of indiscriminate parking and to better manage provision of parking by private developments to support our car-lite vision, however, we need to also calibrate the regulations, monitor and evaluate the parking measures if this invariably results in less take-up of bicycle sharing as a result of this Bill.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: On bike-sharing operators, I have the following concerns.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Licensing for bicycle-sharing operators is a good idea.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: However, LTA must also look into the size of each operator's fleet.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: While there must be regulations, it should not be a deterrent to the market players with high barriers to entry.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Industry players currently operate in a free market.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Yet, with fairly many regulations, these operators may not have the incentive to compete to expand their market size, as well as to invest in innovation for more efficient operation methods if their business is not viable.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: However, the responsibility should not lie solely with the operators, but also with the end user.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Having said that, imposing fines as punitive measures alone may not be the best idea to discourage adverse behaviour, but rather to reward good positive behaviour.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: One of the operators, Ofo, has designed a reward scheme for users who parked the bicycle properly.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: This reward scheme can be practised by other operators to encourage and incentivise correct behaviours.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Operators may be pressured to exit the industry while new entrants may be discouraged with financial penalty imposed on them.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Also, will LTA have plans to ramp up on public education on car sharing to complement and encourage Singaporeans to go green?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: On managing provision of parking by private developments, I have the following concerns.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: On reduced supply of parking lots, will this translate to an increase in car park charges?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Part 4, provision on parking charges, indicates parking charges may be changed from time to time.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Is there any general guideline on the fluctuations?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Is there an upper or lower limit to this?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Does a two-kilometre (km) radius of a train station location constitute the required proximity?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Will there be feeder bus services available in such a situation for those who wish to take public transport?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Lastly, I would like to propose for the Government to encourage and incentivise developers' partnership with private operators.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Such partnership will help to retain the connectivity and convenience of movement around the private development and/or access to public transport.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Developers can be incentivised to partner with operators to provide bike-sharing facilities within the infrastructure development, that it, having designated bicycle parking lots near the building.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Some users seemed to be gripped by a reckless penchant for destruction.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Instead of parking, they are dumping the bicycles and creating junkyards within the city, parks and housing estates.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Will the operators have to rent the parking zones from LTA and, if so, will the cost be passed on to the users?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: For example, if someone takes a photo of a static QR code at a geo-tagged location, it can be reused at a different location, thus defeating the purpose.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: QR codes can also be vandalised, rendering them useless.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I hope the Minister can share more details about the QR code technology that LTA is planning to implement in making space for these bicycle operators.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I hope LTA would not do so at the expense of the parking space currently allotted to those who own their own bicycles.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Many of these are now located near MRT stations, and I hope these will stay put.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Another solution to encourage users to park appropriately would be to create more parking options in places where there is a high volume of usage.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: As bus interchanges, MRT stations and HDB and private housing estates are common destination stops, more purpose-built metal bicycle racks and parking areas could be built as official geo-tagged parking zones.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: These parking zones should preferably be covered so that when it rains, the bicycle seats would not be soaked.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Next, I ask that bicycle parking zones be made available in the industrial estates as some of the workers are frequent bicycle users.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It is good that LTA is working with bicycle-sharing operators to educate bicycle users and develop educational materials on proper bicycle etiquette.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The ugly truth is that some users simply disregard proper etiquette.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: (In Mandarin):   Another solution to encourage users to park appropriately would be to create more parking options in places where there is a high volume of usage.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: As bus interchanges, MRT stations and HDB and private housing estates are common destination stops, more purpose-built metal bicycle racks and parking areas could be built as official geo-tagged parking zones.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: These parking zones should preferably be covered so that when it rains the bicycle seats would not be soaked.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Next, I ask that bicycle parking zones be made available in the industrial estates as some of the workers are frequent bicycle users.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It is good that LTA is working with bicycle-sharing operators to educate bicycle users and develop educational materials on proper bicycle etiquette.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The ugly truth is that some users simply disregard proper etiquette.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Many of the provisions are much needed and timely.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: In particular, I strongly support the installation of proposed QR code for all public bicycle parking points.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Having a clearly defined area to park will do much to manage the situation of indiscriminate parking.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Having said that, I do hope that we can work with the companies to come up with sufficient parking points.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: This is especially in the case of the private estates.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: A key benefit of shared bicycles is the ability to solve the "last-mile problem" in transportation, and this is especially the case with private estates.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: As such, I hope that, especially within our private estates, we can aim for having parking areas near major bus stops, as well as parking areas between every few streets.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: We can allow the bike-sharing companies to propose such locations, given that they know their customer base well, and then have LTA review them to ensure a certain amount of universal coverage.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Given that public behaviour is evolving, it is also important that we regularly review our regulations after the regulations are passed.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: I would also like to ask the Government when it is time we will do a review on this current situation.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: This compares to 0.1 lots in Seoul and zero in Sydney.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Consequently, the car park rate in the Singapore CBD is comparatively cheaper than other major cities in the world.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: This was lower than $919 per month in Hong Kong and Tokyo and seven times lower than $1,338 in London for that year.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: However, I note that under the Range-based Car Parking Standards, developers already have the flexibility to reduce the parking provision for commercial and residential buildings by up to 20% in Zones 1 and 2.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Zone 1 refers to the buildings in the CBD and Zone 2 refers to areas within 400 metres' radius from the MRT stations outside Zone 1.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: In view of the push for a car-lite society, it is understandable for the Ministry of Transport (MOT) to remove the minimum parking lots required for residential and commercial buildings.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: With the current amendment Bill, MOT is stipulating a maximum number of parking lots, instead of a minimum required for each building.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: While I can understand the benefits of replacing car park lots with more commercial space at office buildings and shopping centres, I am more sceptical about the benefits for the buyers of residential units, unless there is a corresponding change in the building codes.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Thus, I would like to clarify a few points with the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: If so, would the Minister mandate a certain percentage of the extra space to benefit the public and the community?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: For example, the windfall arising from having to provide fewer carpark spaces can be shared with the public by providing the additional space for bicycle parking, car sharing/electric car charging facilities, or lease extra space for use to childcare centres or eldercare centres at a cost-recovery rate.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: As a guide, I would like to suggest that MOT consider working with the Ministry of National Development (MND) to direct the building owners to share at least 50% of the benefits arising from the lower car park provision.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: The lower car park provision should also translate to facilities that can benefit members of the public.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: And for new commercial buildings, the lower car park provision should also translate to facilities that also benefit the public, such as promotion of healthy living, promotion of car-lite measures and provision of childcare and eldercare facilities at a cost recovery rate.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Next, will the new parking provision be applicable to existing residential buildings as well?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: If so, would the Minister mandate a certain percentage of the newly available space for use as shared bicycle or PMD parking facilities?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Or for that matter, devote space for car-sharing and electric car charging facilities?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: In a similar fashion, the lower car park provision for the new residential buildings should not end up benefiting the developers alone, and alone.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: I know that developers are capable of maximising the residential units for sale so as to maximise their profits.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Hence, I hope that MOT could work with MND to mandate the bulk of the additional space arising from lower car park provisions for communal spaces like gardens, physical fitness facilities and even shared car, bicycle or PMD parking facilities.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: (In Mandarin):   I would like to applaud MOT's intention to control the abuse and indiscriminate parking of shared bicycles.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: The chief benefit of shared bikes is that they can be parked anywhere, anytime.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Many residents use them to go from HDB void decks to the MRT stations before going to work or school.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: If after the amendment is passed, residents have to walk several hundred metres to use the bikes, it will be taking a step backwards.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: It will depend on how the Minister could shape the situation.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Perhaps the Minister can consider doubling the number of bicycle parking places in two years.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Providing yellow boxes incurs cost and resources, especially when there is a plan to install a unique QR code for each of the yellow boxes.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Such costs should not be completely borne by the Government, Town Councils or building owners.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Only by doing this can the shared-bike operators appreciate the efforts made by the Government.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Not only are vehicles parked this way becoming eyesores on our landscape, they also contribute to obstruction on pavements, passageways and at the entrances and exits of buildings and estates, posing a hazard.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: There are two main problems here: one is the problem of the parking infrastructure, and the other, the problem of accountability.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Mandating the installation of QR codes for approved parking areas will go a long way towards ensuring that these bikes will be deposited where they will not cause disamenities.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Having designated parking lots will also enable the rental firms to collect the bikes more easily in a timely manner when needed.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, we need more designated parking lots in a wider spread of locations to ensure the viability and utilisation of shared bikes.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: LTA has indicated its commitment to enhance our parking infrastructure and I urge the agency to expedite the setting up of more dedicated parking places to facilitate responsible parking.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Areas with significant human traffic, in particular, should have more designated parking areas for these bikes.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Next, I would like to speak on the issues of accountability in Mandarin.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Speaker, I just mentioned that the dockless bikes need more dedicated parking places to deter indiscriminate parking.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We must acknowledge that it is not enough to rely on this measure alone.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The sense of responsibility of each user is very important.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: My residents said that indiscriminate parking is akin to littering.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: They said jokingly that indiscriminate parking is not just a 'land' issue; it has also become an "air, sea and land" problem.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: They explained that "sea" means bicycles are dumped in the drains or by the river; "air" means that you even see bikes on trees or left in the corridor of HDB blocks.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In addition to public education to remind users to park responsibly, we should also consider imposing a fine on recalcitrant offenders, or we can reward those who park responsibly.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I think this can send the message more effectively to riders that they must be responsible for the bicycles used.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This data can help us determine the amount of the fines or reward.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: According to my observation, users are from various social strata, and the majority are from the low-income group.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Most of them are young and middle-aged, including students and foreign workers.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The fine should not be set too high and the award should not be too little so that it can achieve a good deterrent or rewarding effect.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Hence, it is wise for the Government to control the operators and the number of bicycles through licensing.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It is a timely one, with better clarity and provisions made on the parking of vehicles in public places.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I support the overall recommendations made in the amendment Bill.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, I have a few clarifications to make and one suggestion to offer.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: First, I wholly support the inclusion of Part 3 that introduces the new sections 8 to 8T.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: These sections provide better clarity on the various provisions made in Part 3 relating to public parking places, licensing requirements and enforcement actions, which are much needed.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Residents I met have expressed their frustrations with shared vehicles and bicycles that have dotted the void decks and green spaces in our estate.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: At the moment, there is still no requirement for private bicycles or PMD owners to register ownership of such vehicles, and if they also indiscriminately park their vehicles in public places, then no enforcement action can be taken on them.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What enforcement actions can be taken on errant or irresponsible users or hirers of shared vehicles?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And since there are numerous users or hirers of shared vehicles, will monetary fines be the only form of enforcement to be meted out to irresponsible users for indiscriminate parking?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Would LTA consider imposing compulsory community work on repeat offenders, for instance?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Third, the requirement for geo-fencing of a shared vehicle operator’s vehicles has been made known to the operators for quite some time, yet no adherence to this requirement has been made and little or no enforcement carried out.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Hence, for the shared vehicle operators, how does LTA plan to impose the standards of performance, such as the use of geofencing technology or monetary fines, to minimise or eradicate indiscriminate parking of the shared vehicles under their licence?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Will vehicle docking systems, for instance, be imposed on these operators should they fail to comply with the requirements for proper parking of their shared vehicles, such as through the use of geofencing technology?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Will current LTA enforcement officers be sufficient to carry out checks to ensure adherence to the required standards of performance by the shared vehicle operators, or will more enforcement officers need to be recruited?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: To elaborate, when such dispatch riders or food deliverers need to deliver whatever items as assigned as part of their job at these buildings or places, they would park their vehicles at a spot in a public area while they go about delivering the items as assigned, since there are no designated parking lots for motorcycles there.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Examples of such buildings are the Development Bank of Singapore (DBS) Building, Marina Bay Sands and Novena Hospital, from what I understand, though I may stand corrected.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: These dispatch riders and food deliverers can be given vehicle stickers or decals that clearly indicate they are delivering items as assigned as part of their job and some leeway can be given to them to park their vehicles at these Interim Parking Lots during such work assignments.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Operators who manage their fleet well can apply to LTA to grow their fleet.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This will ensure that they grow their fleet sizes in a more sustainable manner and are incentivised to put in place measures to manage the indiscriminate parking as they grow their fleet.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA will use a bottom-up approach and consider each application on its own merits.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This is because the fleet size needs to take into account how well each operator manages his business to maximise utilisation and minimise disamenities.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: With LTA managing the fleet size of each operator, operators will be incentivised to deploy their limited fleet wisely, instead of flooding public bicycle spaces with unused shared bicycles.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA will also monitor the situation and, if necessary, step up the expansion of bicycle infrastructure.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Second, LTA will be able to impose licence conditions as well as set industry-wide standards, to address indiscriminate parking.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Mr Faisal Manap asked about the data requirements under the new section 8K.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Section 8K imposes obligations on operators to keep accounts and records, and to provide information to LTA.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This can include data on the location of each deployed vehicle, so that LTA can track indiscriminate parking and enforce more effectively by leveraging data and technology.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA will put in place safeguards to protect the information, including implementing controls to limit access to the database.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: To ensure that dockless bicycle-sharing remains attractive to users, and to prevent indiscriminate parking, several Members spoke about the importance of having adequate parking, and I agree.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: While it is not possible for us to always have parking at our doorsteps, we are striving to have parking spaces available within a short walk of most households and key destinations.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Currently, there are over 170,000 bicycle parking spaces which are well-distributed across Singapore.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: More than 99% of public homes and 90% of private homes are within a five-minute walk from bicycle parking.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: There are also public bicycle parking areas close to more than 80% of key destinations, such as polyclinics, community centres, schools and town centres.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We will continue to work with HDB, Town Councils and other public agencies to provide more parking spaces where there is demand.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: To address Ms Joan Pereira’s suggestion of sheltered bicycle parking, we will try to locate bicycle parking spaces within sheltered areas as far as possible.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: However, this may not always be possible in areas with site constraints.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Ms Joan Pereira will also be pleased to note that in industrial estates and business parks, JTC has already designated more than 50 parking zones for shared bicycles.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA will continue to work with JTC to implement more parking spaces in industrial areas.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The data that the operators provide to LTA on the distribution of shared bicycles will also help us better plan parking provision, including providing more bicycle parking spaces at areas with high demand.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I share Ms Thanaletchimi's view that the provision of shared device parking in private developments would improve convenience for their tenants and visitors.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA is working with the operators to have them reach out to condominium managements, foreign worker dormitory operators and commercial buildings to allow for the parking of shared devices within these developments.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: However, the decision to allow shared devices to be parked within their premises ultimately rests with the private developers.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: QR codes will be installed at all public parking spaces at MRT stations, bus stops, parks and HDB estates.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Private users can continue to park their bicycles at these spaces as they currently do today, and operators do not have to rent these parking spaces.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Allowing shared bicycles to be parked at public parking places benefits members of the public who use these services.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Ms Joan Pereira also asked about how QR code-enabled geofencing would work and whether its potential downsides can be mitigated.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: QR codes complement the accuracy of GPS-based geofencing.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Safeguards will be put in place to reasonably ensure that the scanning of static QR code geofencing cannot be "gamed".

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: For example, if users take a photo of a QR code and use it to park anywhere outside of the specified parking location, they will not be able to end their trip because the QR code does not match with the GPS location of the shared bicycle.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Where a QR code has been vandalised, users will still be allowed to end their trip if they take a photograph of their bicycle parked within the bicycle parking area and submit it within the operator’s application.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA will also act promptly to replace QR codes which have been damaged.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: At the same time, LTA will continue to study other ways of geofencing to strengthen our capabilities to pinpoint the location of shared bicycles.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Third, Ms Joan Pereira, Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Dr Intan Mokhtar spoke about the measures which will be put in place to engender greater user responsibility.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: With this function, users can plan ahead for where to park before they start their journey.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Despite this, there are still irresponsible users who choose to park indiscriminately.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In other words, irresponsible users who park indiscriminately will continue to be charged until they park properly.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh suggested that the Government hold users accountable for improper parking, instead of relying on operators to do so.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Under the Street Works Act, LTA can fine users who are identified as parking improperly.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: However, it is often difficult to catch users red-handed.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As operators can track the whereabouts of their bicycles, they are better-placed to detect and prevent indiscriminate parking from occurring in the first place.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Nevertheless, LTA will continue to see how we can better enforce against improper parking under the Street Works Act, including using information from the operators to identify hotspots for enforcement.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh also suggested differentiating the fine amounts for individuals based on age and income.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: It is not possible to do so as the law has to be fair to all individuals who have committed the same offence.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Ms Joan Pereira suggested imposing a fine on users who are caught using someone else’s identity to rent a vehicle when they have been banned, while Dr Intan Mokhtar suggested compulsory community work for repeat offenders.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Ms Thanaletchimi asked if LTA could consider waiving the financial penalties for operators who have done their due diligence to discourage users from parking indiscriminately.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Users will be penalised for parking indiscriminately through the collective ban.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Through geofencing, if users do not return their vehicle to a proper parking area, they will not be able to end their trip and will continue to be charged by the operators.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: However, LTA will take regulatory action against the operators if they do not remove the indiscriminately parked vehicles in a timely manner, and if they do not comply with other licence conditions, such as implementing the collective ban.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: To address Dr Intan Mokhtar's query on enforcement resources, we will use data and technology to enforce more efficiently.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We will also cross-deploy enforcement officers where possible, to balance between sufficient enforcement presence on the ground for deterrence as well as the need for prudence and efficiency.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Mr Ang Wei Neng asked about recovering from the operators the costs of the licensing regime, including the cost of providing yellow boxes and QR codes.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We have invested in providing bicycle parking spaces to support active mobility and our car-lite vision.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Hence, we do not intend to charge operators for rental of surface-level bicycle parking spaces and will continue to allow residents who use both private and shared devices, to use these spaces.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Under the licensing regime, LTA can require the operators to provide additional parking spaces if needed.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As far as possible, we intend to recover the costs of the licensing regime through licence fees.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Ms Thanaletchimi cautioned that the licensing regime should not result in high barriers to entry and innovation.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We do not intend for the licensing regime to be unduly onerous for operators.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: However, the licensing requirements are costs which should be internalised by the operators in the course of their business as they reflect the social disamenities caused and efforts needed to address them.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA will monitor their performance closely before determining whether to grant them a full licence.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We agree with Mr Henry Kwek that is it important that our regulations evolve to keep up with public behaviour as well as new technology and business models.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The proposed licensing regime was developed based on feedback on indiscriminate parking from members of the public, LTA’s engagement with stakeholders and interest groups, and the passionate debates we have had here in Parliament.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We will continue to track the situation and engage the public and operators to review the effectiveness of these regulations.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Where necessary, we can also update the licensing conditions to better address indiscriminate bicycle parking.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Some Members have also raised other issues which lie outside the scope of this Bill.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: It is not intended to address issues unrelated to parking, such as reckless riding behaviour and cycling path improvements, which were raised by Dr Teo Ho Pin, and maintenance standards and liability issues in the event of accidents, which were raised by Mr Faisal Manap.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: However, I understand these are useful and pertinent suggestions.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The Active Mobility Advisory Panel will be reviewing the active mobility rules to address reckless riding.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: To address indiscriminate parking of privately-owned bicycles, we will continue to provide more parking spaces and step up enforcement where necessary.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Developments within 400 metres of an MRT station, for example, are considered to be well-connected via public transport.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: For areas which are more than 400 metres away from an MRT station, there is already an extensive feeder bus network to provide first-and-last mile connectivity.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Ms Thanaletchimi also asked about the impact of the new parking provision parking charges.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Private parking charges are determined by the market, and may vary based on the specific parking demand, parking availability and building owners’ parking management considerations.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As for HDB and URA’s parking charges, HDB and URA takes into account relevant factors, such as the costs of providing car parks, when setting car park charges at a reasonable level.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: For existing developments undergoing redevelopment or major A&A works, LTA will work closely with URA to implement the new parking standards and to ensure that our limited land resources are put to good use.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: With regard to Dr Intan Mokhtar's suggestion on provision of parking spaces for despatch riders, LTA will study its feasibility.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Since our last review of the car parking provision requirements, there has been a significant expansion of the public transport network and enhancement in first- and last-mile connectivity.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In summary, Mr Speaker, this Bill seeks to support car-lite initiatives in a sustainable and responsible manner.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The amendments to vehicle parking provision will enable us to calibrate vehicle parking more precisely, so that we can maximise the use of the limited land in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: With that, Mr Speaker, I beg to move.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: Because the Senior Minister of State mentioned we will be providing yellow boxes within a five-minute walking distance to the units.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We also have to take into consideration the demand for shared bicycle services.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: If the demand is high, then we will draw more boxes.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This is one area where we can actually make use of the data submitted by the bike-sharing operators to determine exactly where the high-demand areas are, and we will draw yellow boxes accordingly.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Chairman, there are five amendments to clause 5, as indicated in the Order Paper Supplement.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As the amendments are related, may I seek your permission to move them together?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Chairman, I beg to move the amendments 1 to 5* standing in the Minister's name, as indicated in the Order Paper Supplement.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Chairman, I beg to move that the amendment* standing in the Minister's name, as indicated in the Order Paper Supplement.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Chairman, I beg to move that the amendments* standing in the Minister's name, as indicated in the Order Paper Supplement.
